skill.name: context-degradation
skill.description: Diagnoses context degradation in LLM agents, including lost-in-middle failures, poisoning, distraction, confusion, clash, and attention-related performance decline.
skill.summary: Detect context failure patterns and select practical mitigation strategies.
skill.author: muratcankoylan

security_audit.summary: All 22 static findings are false positives caused by Python documentation markup, Markdown formatting, ordinary text literals, and a benign dictionary-key print. No command execution, credential handling, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or other malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Explaining foundational context mechanics without an active failure: `context-fundamentals`.
- Applying token-efficiency tactics after the failure pattern is known: `context-optimization`.
- Designing a compression or handoff summary strategy: `context-compression`.
- Persisting large outputs, logs, or scratch state outside the prompt: `filesystem-context`.
- `context-fundamentals`: conceptual explanation of attention and context windows before a failure e
- `context-optimization`: masking, caching, partitioning, and other token-efficiency tactics after d
- `context-compression`: structured summaries and handoffs when accumulated context must be compacte
- `filesystem-context`: offloading raw outputs, logs, and scratch state so poisoned or bulky context
- `multi-agent-patterns`: isolating tasks into separate contexts to prevent confusion and clash.

content.value_statement: Long contexts can hide critical instructions, preserve bad claims, and mix conflicting tasks. This skill diagnoses the failure pattern and recommends placement, filtering, compression, isolation, or recovery strategies.
actual_capabilities: Classifies failures as lost-in-middle, poisoning, distraction, confusion, or clash.
Estimates attention distribution across context positions with a demonstrative U-shaped model.
Flags critical items placed in attention-degraded regions.
Detects heuristic poisoning indicators, contradictions, and uncertain claim markers.
Produces a composite context health score with mitigation recommendations.
limitations: Attention values are simulated and do not inspect model internals.
Token counts use whitespace splitting instead of model-specific tokenizers.
Poisoning detection relies on simple patterns and can produce false positives.
Published degradation thresholds require validation against each model and workload.

use_cases.title: Debug a Long Agent Session
use_cases.description: Identify why instructions or facts stop influencing responses as conversation history grows.

use_cases.title: Review Retrieved Context
use_cases.description: Find irrelevant, outdated, contradictory, or unverified material before it enters a model prompt.

use_cases.title: Design Reliability Tests
use_cases.description: Define workload-specific baselines, degradation thresholds, monitoring signals, and recovery checks.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Context Diagnosis
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this conversation for context degradation. Identify the likely pattern, cite symptoms, and recommend three immediate fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an agent starts producing irrelevant or inconsistent responses.

prompt_templates.title: Lost-in-Middle Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the supplied prompt layout for lost-in-middle risk. Mark critical content, assess placement, and propose a safer ordering.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before sending a long assembled prompt to a model.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieval Quality Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these documents for poisoning, distraction, and clash. Explain source conflicts, relevance gaps, and content that should be removed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a retrieval pipeline returns mixed or conflicting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Production Health Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a context health plan for this agent. Define metrics, baselines, alert thresholds, compaction triggers, recovery steps, and validation tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when building production monitoring for a long-running agent.

output_examples.input: The agent ignores a deadline placed halfway through a long project history.
output: Move the deadline into the current task block and repeat it near the prompt end.
Retest at increasing context lengths to confirm the placement effect.

output_examples.input: Two retrieved guides describe different API endpoints, and the agent alternates between them.
output: Likely pattern: context clash caused by version conflict.
Label each source version and select the production version before prompt assembly.
Exclude the outdated guide and record the precedence decision.

best_practices: Establish a low-context performance baseline before diagnosing degradation.
Keep source provenance and version labels beside every retrieved claim.
Trigger compaction or isolation before measured performance reaches its decline threshold.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one weak response as proof of context degradation.
Do not add corrections while leaving known poisoned claims in context.
Do not assume advertised context capacity guarantees workload quality.

faq.question: What degradation patterns does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers lost-in-middle, poisoning, distraction, confusion, and clash.

faq.question: Does it measure real model attention?
faq.answer: No. The included detector simulates a U-shaped distribution for demonstration.

faq.question: Can it detect every poisoned claim?
faq.answer: No. It uses heuristic markers and requires human or model-assisted verification.

faq.question: When should I split work across agents?
faq.answer: Use isolation when tasks have separate goals, constraints, tools, or conflicting context.

faq.question: How should I choose a compaction threshold?
faq.answer: Benchmark your workload and trigger compaction before its measured degradation point.

faq.question: Does this replace model-specific evaluation?
faq.answer: No. Model versions and workloads require separate tests and updated thresholds.
